regime_context: Memory, HBM & Storage leads momentum ranks but with fading strength, zero breadth, and mixed trend health. The absolute-trend gate is beneficial for drawdown control. Several eligible themes show durable, broad trends without crowding—most notably Financials and Energy—while crowded ones like Cybersecurity remain intact but carry positioning risk. The rotation radar shows a narrow leader margin but provides no predictive signal.

theses.subject: Financials (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: The theme passes the absolute-trend gate with high durability (0.83) and broad participation (89.5%), and is not crowded. The validated drawdown-control edge supports a trend-following stance here.
theses.dissent: Financials are macro-sensitive; a sudden recession scare or yield-curve inversion reversal could rapidly unwind the trend.

falsifier.text: XLF weekly close below its 20-day simple moving average.

theses.subject: Energy (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: The theme is trending with moderate breadth and no crowding, and eligibility indicates the absolute-trend gate finds sustained price persistence. The drawdown-control edge favors staying with the trend.
theses.dissent: As a cyclical energy play, any sharp drop in crude oil or global demand fears could abruptly reverse the uptrend.

falsifier.text: XLE weekly close below its 50-day simple moving average.

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity shows the strongest trend quality—full breadth, high durability—but is heavily crowded. Crowding is a size-down caution, not a fade signal; the absolute-trend gate still supports trend-following discipline.
theses.dissent: Extreme crowding often precedes sharp, fast drawdowns on any negative catalyst, possibly breaching the trend gate’s typical risk control.

falsifier.text: CIBR daily close below its 21-day exponential moving average, or a single session loss >3% on above-average volume that undercuts the prior week’s low.

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
